title: BEGINNER LINE DANCE - COWBOY HUSTLE - TUTORIAL!

method.teacher_system: The teacher breaks the dance into small, manageable chunks, demonstrating each one clearly from a back view. She then combines these chunks into a sequence, repeating the full routine multiple times to ensure the learner can follow along. Finally, she performs the dance to music to demonstrate the full flow.
method.signature: The teacher uses a back view throughout the entire lesson, allowing learners to copy her movements directly without needing to mentally mirror them.

practices.what: The teacher breaks down the initial fan motion with the right foot, explaining the out-in-out-in pattern.
The teacher introduces the heel and toe taps, breaking them down into forward and backward movements.
The teacher teaches the step-kick and step-touch sequence, repeating it twice.
The teacher explains the grapevine step, breaking it down into a side-behind-side-touch pattern.
The teacher leads a full run-through of the entire dance sequence from the beginning.

adaptations.difficulty: The hop step might be too challenging for some.
adaptations.adjustment: The teacher offers a simpler step-out and step-back alternative.

beliefs.belief: Line dancing is versatile and can be performed to almost any country song.

feelings.response: The teacher acknowledges that the steps can be confusing and suggests repeating the sequence multiple times.
The teacher acknowledges the potential for confusion and offers to repeat the sequence to help the learner.

moments.says: The teacher introduces herself and the dance, emphasizing that it is very basic and can be done to almost any song.
The teacher acknowledges that the next part can be confusing and suggests practicing it multiple times.
The teacher says it can get confusing if you don't do it lots of times, and then repeats the sequence.
The teacher confirms the steps are taught and reminds the learner to add the quarter turn at the end.
The teacher offers a choice between a more energetic hop or a simpler step-out-and-back.
The teacher encourages the learner to try the dance and watch the next demo to see what song to use.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable and encouraged to practice, knowing the dance is simple and fun.

struggles.theme: Difficulty following instructors in live classes

clicked.theme: The back view makes it easy to copy

meant.theme: Helps with therapy and physical rehabilitation
Provides confidence to dance in public

method.limits: The video does not provide on-screen text for counts or step names, relying entirely on verbal instruction.
